change: Add a reusable authored effect-clock workload and two behavior regressions. Evaluate and reject two native clock storage implementations; retain the existing production implementation.
decision: Neither candidate justifies replacing the current clock path. The first has mixed clock results and two substantial actor-workload regressions. The typed-handle revision increases CPU cycles in all three getter-heavy clock pairs (about 2.5% to 15.3%). Chart or actor improvements do not justify that generic script regression. Production changes were reverted; no chart-specific fallback was introduced.
baseline_method: Build the clean starting revision before edits, then each candidate with the same pinned compiler, profile, dependencies and runner. Three adjacent before/after pairs per workload and candidate, alternating variant order. All runs retained.
build: Normal dev profile, song-lua/mlua opt-level 3. No test-support or song-lua-performance feature in measured binaries.

measurement.cpu_cycles: QueryThreadCycleTime on the pinned gameplay update thread.
measurement.throughput: Median headless gameplay updates/second; includes live Lua and visual publication, excludes observation hashing. This is not rendered FPS.
measurement.allocations: Rust GlobalAlloc across all threads in the measured process, including mlua. Direct native malloc is excluded. Reallocations are reported separately.
measurement.allocated_bytes: Allocation and reallocation traffic during updates, not retained memory, peak heap or RSS.
measurement.environment: Serial runs; no concurrent agent builds/tests, no GUI, GPU or audio-device initialization. Small timing differences remain noisy.

timing_interpretation: Report percentages of medians and median adjacent-pair changes separately. Three pairs are limited samples; timing varies between runs. These results do not establish general chart speedups. Allocation bytes are traffic, not retained memory or peak heap.

experiments.implementation: Owned userdata clock; each getter and mutation performs a scoped native borrow through Lua.

validation.visual_fingerprints: All 48 runs have matching visual fingerprints for their workload, across baseline and both candidates. Hashing covers every pose and mesh/text/texture payload after every update, outside timing. This does not establish pixel rendering or complete ITGmania parity.
validation.candidate_tests: 41 selected tests passed for each measured candidate, including clock snapshot independence, restarts, float values, table fallbacks and zero allocation churn after slot creation.
validation.retained_behavior_tests: Timer boundary/single-subtraction behavior and public getters; live/table-backed execution through effect switches, timer/music/beat changes, hibernation, update rates, zero and large deltas, spin/tweens, draw snapshots and InitState.
validation.production_verification: Removing the two new cfg(test) blocks reconstructs the baseline Rust source after newline normalization. Host/lib were restored exactly and the candidate clock module was removed.

native_replay.result: Initial candidate only: known failure, byte-identical to baseline, with 12,519 draw mismatches starting at frame 226. Not a passing parity result. Production was ultimately restored to baseline. No fixture regeneration or ITGmania edits.

source_identity_followup.finding: The reported mismatches used an installed simfile with a different offset from the capture. Verified original sources pass Single and Versus; those historical mismatches are not evidence of an engine defect.

normal_application_build.result: passed with the retained test-only changes

reference.reviewed_behavior: Actor::UpdateInternal advances effect clocks before spin/tweening. Timer clocks subtract the period only once when units are strictly greater than the period. Global/music/beat delta is new time minus previous effect time.

next_step: Investigate binding actor methods and the update loop directly to stable native actor slots, so clock operations avoid repeated Lua userdata lookup and ownership/locking work. Re-measure before retaining a migration.
remaining_work: Rotation still shares state with the separate spin queue and retains its Lua synchronization.
Immediate non-tween scalar properties remain Lua-backed.
Preparation fields remain for compiler/adapter compatibility; migrated live writes no longer refresh them.
Live frame snapshots and visual publication copies remain. This does not complete the one-slot actor architecture.
